context: A triptych showing one 40-node, 5-group network three ways: force-directed layout (left), radial edge bundling (center), and chord diagram aggregated by group (right), with linked hover highlighting across all three panels.
first_impression: The three-panel layout is cohesive and the 5-color Tol palette keeps categories distinguishable, but the radial edge bundling panel's node labels become illegible where nodes cluster at the bottom arc.
what_works: The chord diagram cleanly summarizes group-level flow with only 5 ribbons and well-separated arcs; the linked dispatch that dims non-relevant elements across all panels on hover is cognitively sound — it converts three independent views into a single focused query.
what_doesnt: Radial bundling labels for Thalamus nodes (bottom arc) overlap severely at 8px and are unreadable without interaction, undermining the panel's ability to convey node identity; the force-directed layout's cluster separation is loose enough that the five groups read more as a scattered cloud than five distinct communities until a node is hovered.
